translations.idiomatic: He gathered many brocade workers at his official residence to weave fine silks. Whenever he needed something he took it from the market and only paid half a year later, and also had his retainers seize goods on the side.

sentences.zh: 廣糴黍稻，未及成熟者亦取之，悉貯寺觀中，久之損敗，即勒道釋償之。

translations.literal: He bought up millet and rice in large quantities, taking even crops not yet ripe; he stored it all in temples and monasteries, and when it rotted after a long time he forced monks and Taoists to compensate for it.
translations.idiomatic: He bought up millet and rice in large quantities, taking even crops not yet ripe. He stored it all in temples and monasteries, and when it rotted after a long time he forced monks and Taoists to compensate for the loss.

sentences.zh: 縱其下淩忽軍校。

translations.literal: He let his subordinates bully and insult military officers.
translations.idiomatic: He let his subordinates bully and insult military officers.

sentences.zh: 劍南自李順平後，人心洶洶，知州牛冕緩馳無政，昭壽又不能御軍，人皆怨憤。

translations.literal: After Li Shun was pacified in southern Shu, popular sentiment was turbulent; Prefect Niu Mian was lax and slow in governance; Zhaoshou also could not control the army; everyone harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Shun was pacified in southern Shu, popular sentiment was turbulent. Prefect Niu Mian was lax and slow in governance, and Zhaoshou also could not control the army. Everyone harbored resentment.

sentences.zh: 神衛卒趙延順等八人謀，欲害昭壽，未敢發。

translations.literal: Eight palace guard soldiers including Zhao Yanshun plotted to kill Zhaoshou but did not yet dare act.
translations.idiomatic: Eight palace guard soldiers including Zhao Yanshun plotted to kill Zhaoshou but did not yet dare act.

sentences.zh: 三年正旦，中使自峨眉山還京，昭壽戒馭吏具鞍馬將送之，延順等悉解廄中馬韁，奔逸庭下，陽逐喧呼，登廳執昭壽殺之，並殺二僕，據甲仗庫，取兵器。

translations.literal: On New Year's Day of the third year, a palace envoy returning from Emei Mountain to the capital — Zhaoshou ordered his attendants to prepare saddles and horses to send him off. Yanshun and the others all loosened the reins of the horses in the stables; the horses bolted into the courtyard. Pretending to pursue them with shouts, they mounted the hall, seized Zhaoshou and killed him along with two servants, occupied the armory, and took weapons.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day of the third year, a palace envoy was returning from Emei Mountain to the capital. Zhaoshou ordered his attendants to prepare saddles and horses to send him off. Yanshun and the others all loosened the reins of the horses in the stables, and the horses bolted into the courtyard. Pretending to pursue them with shouts, they mounted the hall, seized Zhaoshou and killed him along with two servants, occupied the armory, and took weapons.

sentences.zh: 都監王澤聞之，急召本軍都虞候王均率兵擒捕。

translations.literal: Overall supervisor Wang Ze heard of this and urgently summoned the chief adjutant of the local army Wang Jun to lead troops and capture them.
translations.idiomatic: Overall supervisor Wang Ze heard of this and urgently summoned the chief adjutant of the local army, Wang Jun, to lead troops and capture them.

sentences.zh: 延順左執昭壽首，右操劍，仿徨無所適，卒見均至，即與眾推均為帥，合驍猛、威武兵為亂。

translations.literal: Yanshun held Zhaoshou's head in his left hand and a sword in his right, wandering with nowhere to go; when Jun arrived they immediately pushed Jun as commander, and the Tiger Fierce and Martial Prestige troops combined in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshun held Zhaoshou's head in his left hand and a sword in his right, wandering with nowhere to go. When Jun arrived they immediately pushed Jun as commander, and the Tiger Fierce and Martial Prestige troops combined in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 牛冕洎轉運使張適奔漢州。

translations.literal: Niu Mian and the transport commissioner Zhang Shi fled to Hanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Mian and the transport commissioner Zhang Shi fled to Hanzhou.

sentences.zh: 是秋，官兵討平之。

translations.literal: That autumn government troops suppressed the rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn government troops suppressed the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 見《雷有終傳》。

translations.literal: See the biography of Lei Youzhong.
translations.idiomatic: See the biography of Lei Youzhong.

sentences.zh: 昭壽子承諒，娶齊王女嘉興縣主，至內殿承制。

translations.literal: Zhaoshou's son Chengliang married the Princess of Jiaxing, daughter of the Prince of Qi, and rose to director of memorials within the Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoshou's son Chengliang married the Princess of Jiaxing, daughter of the Prince of Qi, and rose to director of palace memorials within the Hall.

sentences.zh: 論曰：五季之亂，內則權臣擅命，外則藩鎮握兵。

translations.literal: The commentary says: In the chaos of the Five Dynasties, within the realm powerful ministers usurped command; outside, military governors held armed power.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: In the chaos of the Five Dynasties, powerful ministers usurped command within the realm while military governors held armed power without.

sentences.zh: 宋興，內外廓清，若天去其疾，或納節以備宿衛，或請老以奉朝請。

translations.literal: When Song rose, within and without were cleared; it was as if heaven removed its affliction. Some surrendered their seals to serve as palace guards; some requested retirement to attend court audiences.
translations.idiomatic: When Song rose, within and without were cleared, as if heaven had removed its affliction. Some surrendered their seals to serve as palace guards; others requested retirement to attend regular court audiences.

sentences.zh: 雖太祖善禦，諸臣知機，要亦否極而泰之象也。

translations.literal: Although the founder was skilled at control and the ministers knew the moment, this was also the image of misfortune reaching its limit and turning to peace.
translations.idiomatic: Although the founder was skilled at control and his ministers knew the moment, this was also the image of misfortune reaching its limit and turning to peace.

sentences.zh: 彥卿一門二后，累朝襲寵，有謀善戰，聲振殊俗，與時進退，其名將之賢者歟？

translations.literal: Yanqing's house produced two empresses and enjoyed successive imperial favor; resourceful and skilled in battle, his fame resounded in foreign lands; advancing and withdrawing with the times — was he not among the worthy of famous generals?
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing's house produced two empresses and enjoyed successive imperial favor. Resourceful and skilled in battle, his fame resounded in foreign lands, and he advanced and withdrew with the times — was he not among the worthy of famous generals?

sentences.zh: 令坤、延釗素與太祖親善，平荊、湘則南服底定，鎮常山則北邊載寧，未嘗恃舊與功以啟嫌隙。

translations.literal: Lingkun and Yanzhao had long been on intimate terms with the founder; pacifying Jing and Xiang stabilized the south, holding Changshan kept the north secure — they never relied on old ties and merit to provoke suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Lingkun and Yanzhao had long been on intimate terms with the founder. Pacifying Jing and Xiang stabilized the south, and holding Changshan kept the north secure. They never relied on old ties and past merit to provoke suspicion.

sentences.zh: 創業君臣有過人者，類如是夫。

translations.literal: The founding emperor and his ministers surpassed ordinary men in such ways.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor and his ministers surpassed ordinary men in such ways.
